message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
**This ECG appears to show sinus rhythm at about 65 beats/minute with a left bundle branch block (LBBB)**—a delay in electrical activation of the left ventricle.

My reading from the image:

- Regular rhythm, with a P wave before each QRS.
- Widened QRS complexes, approximately **140–160 ms**, with broad lateral R waves and deep negative complexes in V1–V3, supporting LBBB.
- ST elevation in V1–V3 and ST depression/T-wave changes in lateral leads, mostly opposite the QRS direction. These can be secondary to LBBB. [ECG reference](https://www.merckmanuals.com/en-ca/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/specific-cardiac-arrhythmias/bundle-branch-block-and-fascicular-block?autoredirectid=20568&media=print)

**I don’t see clear modified Sgarbossa criteria for an acute coronary occlusion, but this image cannot rule out a heart attack.** LBBB makes that assessment harder; symptoms, previous ECGs, repeat ECGs, and troponin blood tests matter. [ACC guidance](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10691881/)

If you currently have chest pain, breathlessness, sweating, or fainting, seek emergency care now. If you feel well, arrange clinician review, comparison with an older ECG, and usually an echocardiogram if this LBBB is newly discovered.

What prompted the ECG, and is there a previous tracing for comparison?
